entries.939b7e3972161744: A single-segment business operating a chain of restaurants centered on Japanese cuisine. Revenue for the fiscal year ended February 2026 was ¥9,614 million, and the number of stores at the end of the period was 88. It operates stores in 2 fu and 6 ken: the Kansai area (Osaka, Hyogo, Kyoto and Nara prefectures), the Chubu area (Aichi, Mie and Gifu prefectures), and the Chugoku area (Okayama Prefecture).
entries.a7019a89f4748b9a: A specialty shop serving udon noodles made daily in an in-store noodle-making facility using the Sanuki method, with carefully selected wheat and salt. It also offers omusubi, tempura and oden. The number of stores is 12, and sales for the fiscal year ended February 2026 were ¥1,109 million.
entries.a970a1c2a11eab97: As its medium- to long-term management strategy, it cites active store openings in the Machikadoya format, development of new formats, and scrap-and-build. As roadside store sites decline, it is opening new stores on residential roads and in small trade areas and closing unprofitable stores; under its dominant strategy, it expands stores with an emphasis on profitability and strives to widen its store areas.

It aims to diversify store locations by keeping initial investment low and operating efficiently with a small staff. The number of stores is 7, and sales for the fiscal year ended February 2026 were ¥654 million.
entries.f948855719eda579: Za Meshiya, a cafeteria-style restaurant, offers the enjoyment of 'choice,' letting customers freely combine items from about 120 menu items, and combines the speed of fast-food style with the relaxed atmosphere of a restaurant. The company states that these characteristics, together with the piping-hot, fast service of Machikadoya, which cooks to order, will be the key to surviving in the restaurant industry, where stores are oversupplied.
